messages:
lina: quick heads-up — I found a reproducible read-after-write hole during a demote+prefetch handoff scenario. minimal repro below, logged on a single node.
lina: repro steps:
```
1) client writes key K -> routed to node A (primary)
2) A demotes prefix P and starts async prefetch to node B
3) client immediately issues read for K -> hits node B before prefetch completes
4) B returns stale/missing result
```
lina: this seems to happen when demote returns success before the prefetch commit is applied at the receiver (B), so reads race the in-flight prefill.
ben: saw this in a load test yesterday. I added logging and caught a few requests where A's demote acknowledged at t0 but B's apply completed t0+~120ms.
sam: is the demote API currently synchronous only for the local slab ownership update? iirc we don't wait for the remote ack by design to keep latency bounded.
maria: yep — design was: demote returns after local state flips and we enqueue a prefill RPC. tradeoff was latency vs correctness for immediate reads.
ben: can we piggyback a "prefetch-commit" flag in the demote response to the client? probably not ideal — client changes are messy.
tao: alternative: attach a short-lived commit token to the prefix metadata on A. Any read routed to B without token triggers fetch-from-A (or stalls) — basically fail-open to guarantee read-after-write.
maria: token approach seems lightweight: token only lives for e.g. 500ms-2s. Pros: no global synchronous barrier. Cons: extra branching in read path and slightly more RPCs when token missing.
sam: another option: lease-extension on demote — A holds a soft lease for Xms during which it remains authoritative for reads. B rejects reads until it has applied. That's higher-cost for A-side but simpler semantics.
ben: sequence-number approach: each prefix has a monotonically increasing apply-epoch; reads carry the epoch they observed. Destination refuses reads older than epoch. That feels like the clean long-term model but requires more plumbing and coordination.
maria: tradeoffs summary:
- sync demote+apply ack: simplest correctness, high latency
- commit-token (ephemeral marker): low latency, medium complexity, local-only
- soft lease: correctness with bounded forwarding but increases load on source
- epoch/sequencing: robust, supports multi-dest, higher engineering cost
tao: proposal (short-term): implement ephemeral commit-token + read fallback. Flow:
```
1) A demotes prefix P and issues prefill to B with commit_token=T
2) A returns success and includes token TTL in internal metadata
3) B applies prefill and records T as applied
4) if a read lands on B and T not present, B synchronously issues fetch-from-A (or returns MISS that triggers client retry)
```
tao: this keeps normal fast path unchanged, only pays on the race window.
maria: metrics we should collect immediately: number of reads that hit B without token, fetch-from-A latency, error/retry counts, and token TTL misses. add dashboards.
sam: short-term safety patch: set token TTL to 1s, monitor. If levels are high under tail latency we can raise TTL or flip to soft lease.
ben: long-term: tao + sam should prototype epoched-lease RFC that composes with distributed handoff (we can use apply-epoch + causal read tokens). Aim for RFC in 2 sprints.
lina: sounds good. i'm going to attach my repro logs to the ticket.
infra-bot: deploy:prefetch-shim v2 rolled to staging at 2026-03-18T14:02:00Z :rocket:
maria: action items:
- tao: open RFC for epoched-lease model (assign: tao)
- sam: add token-miss metric + dashboard (assign: sam)
- ben: add integration test that asserts read-after-write in demote case (assign: ben)
- maria: land hotfix for token TTL and monitor (assign: maria)
lina: thanks all — i'll follow up with trace snippets and a small log gadget to reproduce locally. :thumbsup:"
